title: Demonstrative Articles
definition: Demonstrative words point to a particular person or thing, often meaning 'this', 'that', or 'these'. In A1 German, dieser, diese, dieses change according to the noun's gender, number, and case. In everyday speech, das is also commonly used to point something out.

rules.title: Basic forms in the nominative
rules.explanation: Use dieser with masculine nouns, diese with feminine and plural nouns, and dieses with neuter nouns.

rules.title: Pointing with das
rules.explanation: Das ist ... is a very common way to identify or point at something.

examples.german: Was ist das? — Das ist ein Schlüssel.
examples.english: What is that? — That is a key.

examples.german: Wer ist das? — Das ist meine Schwester.
examples.english: Who is that? — That is my sister.

rules.title: Demonstratives in the accusative
rules.explanation: In the accusative, masculine dieser changes to diesen. Feminine diese, neuter dieses, and plural diese stay the same.

rules.title: Demonstratives in the dative
rules.explanation: In the dative, common forms are diesem (masculine/neuter), dieser (feminine), and diesen (plural, usually with -n on the noun if possible).

common_mistakes.explanation: Mann is masculine nominative, so use dieser.

mastery_goal: You can point out people and things and use basic dieser/diese/dieses forms in common cases.
